issue: हरे in line 1: vocative (हे हरे) or verb (हर लिये, carried off) of the beings swayed by māyā
alternatives: verb: all beings, moving and unmoving, are carried off (captured) under the sway of your māyā

issue: प्रिय संत अनंत सदा: अनंत as the Lord (saints and the Lord are dear) or as 'endlessly' qualifying प्रिय
our reading: saints and the infinite Lord are ever dear to them
alternatives: saints are ever dear to them beyond measure

issue: Who is परानंद संदोह: the one who knows the devotee's joy is himself the mass of supreme bliss (the Lord), or one who has attained that bliss?
our reading: only one who is himself a mass of supreme bliss knows his joy (apposition, as the words stand)
alternatives: only one who has attained the supreme bliss (Brahman) knows it; or: the Lord, the mass of supreme bliss, alone knows it

issue: ब्यलीक मद खंडन: 'breaker of false pride' (ब्यलीक qualifying मद) or 'breaker of falsehood and pride' (two objects)

review: Agree: line 1 reads as the narrator's statement and Garuḍa's words begin at line 2, where ताता addresses Bhuśuṇḍi.
Agree: मतिधीर as an address to Garuḍa fits Bhuśuṇḍi's discourse to him; the general reading stays an alternative.

issue: Who says line 1 (गुर बिनु भव निधि तरइ न कोई…): the narrator's comment on Garuḍa's state, or the opening of Garuḍa's own words (he speaks with ताता in line 2)?
our reading: Line 1 as the narrator's general statement; Garuḍa's speech begins at line 2.

issue: मतिधीर: an address to Garuḍa ('O steady-minded one') or the subject of a general maxim ('the steady-minded, considering thus…'); भजहु is imperative plural.
alternatives: General: the steady-minded should give up sophistry and worship Śrī Rāma.

issue: सत पंच चौपाईं: read as 'five or seven caupāīs' (सत = सात), or as 'a hundred and five', or with सत पंच as 'true arbiters' (the caupāīs taken as a true guide).
alternatives: 'a hundred and five caupāīs'; 'knowing the lovely caupāīs to be a true arbiter (सत् पंच)'.

issue: आभीर … स्वपचादि अति अघरूप जे: जे may restrict ('those among them who are sin itself') or describe the whole list ('who are sin itself').
our reading: Restrictive: those among them who are sin itself (the milder sense, per style §2 on groups).
alternatives: Descriptive: the Ābhīras, Yavanas … who are utterly sinful.

issue: राम नमामि ते: ते read as the Sanskrit enclitic 'to you' (address to Rāma) or as 'that' (उन श्रीरामजीको).
our reading: हे राम! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ / Rāma, I bow to you.

issue: दूरि फराक: फराक as 'wide, open' (Persian farākh) or 'apart, separate' (Arabic firāq); not a Sanskrit word, so Monier-Williams and Apte cannot settle it.
our reading: Far off, in an open place, is a fine ghat (फराक = open, spacious).
alternatives: Set apart at some distance (from the other ghats) is that fine ghat.

issue: सकृत (both lines): MW and Apte give only 'once, at once, at one time, always' for सकृत्; the writer's proposed word sense 'scarcely one, rarely' is not a dictionary sense of the word.
our reading: सकृत कोउ = 'just one, a single one' (once, i.e. one in all those millions); 'scarcely one' / कोई एक ही renders this and is kept.
alternatives: If the glossary entry for सकृत is changed, keep 'once' first and give 'a single one (in this idiom)' rather than 'rarely'.

issue: नख करज: Monier-Williams and Apte give करज only as 'finger-nail' (kara-ja, born of the hand); Hindi usage also takes करज as 'finger'. With नख beside it, the line reads as nails and fingers, or nails twice (नख करज = the nails of the hands).
our reading: नख और अँगुलियाँ / nails and fingers (glossary: करज = उँगलियाँ).
alternatives: हाथोंके नख / the nails of his hands (करज qualifying नख), i.e. रोली-से लाल हथेलियाँ और नाखून.

issue: अज बिग्यान रूप बल धामा: our meaning uses रूप twice, as विज्ञानस्वरूप and again as रूप (beauty) in 'रूप तथा बलके धाम'. The words allow either विज्ञानरूप + बलधाम, or विज्ञान, रूप and बल all governed by धाम.
our reading: विज्ञानस्वरूप, और रूप तथा बलके धाम / realised knowledge itself, the abode of beauty and strength.
alternatives: विज्ञानस्वरूप और बलके धाम / realised knowledge itself and the abode of strength; or विज्ञान, रूप और बलके धाम / the abode of knowledge, beauty and strength.

issue: मोह कलिल: is कलिल mire or a thicket/confused mass?
our reading: the mire of delusion (my mind was clogged with it)

issue: त्रिजग: tiryak (animals and birds) or trijagat (the three worlds)? MW has trijagat 'the three worlds'; no headword त्रिजग.
our reading: animals (tiryak beings), listed with gods, humans and asuras
alternatives: all beings of the three worlds, with gods, humans and asuras

issue: बियोग बिसोक हए: MW and Apte give viśoka only as 'free from sorrow' (and 'cessation of sorrow'); neither lists vi- as intensive with śoka. 'Free from sorrow' cannot stand beside हए (smitten), so the line needs बिसोक = वि (intensive / Avadhī) + सोक, which the dictionaries do not confirm.
our reading: struck down by separation and deep grief (review's word fix: विशेष शोक).
alternatives: Read बि- as a plain Avadhī prefix to सोक, 'by separation and grief' without 'deep'.

issue: ब्रह्मगिरा: voice of Brahman (the Lord) or of Brahmā?
our reading: voice of Brahman, the Lord himself, since it calls Bhuśuṇḍi 'my devotee'
alternatives: voice of Brahmā (a heavenly voice in general, as in the glossary's part gloss)

issue: त्रिबिधि ईषना तरुन तिजारी: MW gives taruṇa of a disease as 'just begun' (fresh, acute stage); our pieces say 'raging' / 'प्रचण्ड', which is the Hindi sense 'at its height'.
alternatives: 'an acute (freshly risen) tertian fever' (नयी चढ़ी, तीव्र तिजारी), following the Āyurvedic taruṇa-jvara.
